conclusion: Baseline: the "Reply with only the digits." prompt ran to the 2048 cap (hit_cap true, repeated false — truncation of a self-verifying answer, not a literal token loop), while the same question phrased "Answer with just the number." terminated at 471 tokens. I captured the loop direction at layer 12 (contrast_cosine 0.98, norm 1.0) and a second capture at layer 20 with a token_window past the shared prefix; direction_similarity between them was 0.9995, so the component is reproducible rather than noise, and aligned_columns at both layers pointed at the same small column set (102, 987, 914, 989, 431, 296, 178, 3252, 51, 2107) — columns whose norms are unremarkable, which is why the norm ranking alone would not have found them. I then applied a directional edit to layer 12's down_proj over the contiguous window 900:1000 (which contains the strongest aligned columns 914, 987, 989), subtracting 1.0× the captured direction from those 100 columns (102,400 weights) and reloading from edit_L12_a. After the edit the target prompt terminates at 191 tokens with no cap hit and the answer is still 132 (run_model returns "132"), the control phrasing is unchanged at 471 tokens, and a held-out question (17×23) still answers correctly in 24 tokens — so the edit removes the re-verification without breaking correctness. If I had more budget I would sweep the scale (0.5/1.0/2.0) and narrow the window to the three top columns to confirm this is the minimum sufficient edit.
